podcast.body: A novelty song released in 1956 that used sampling for comedic effect, reaching number three on the Billboard singles charts. Goodman was sued for copyright infringement but was cleared by a judge who declared the work a parody. "Dickie Goodman, an American composer of novelty songs, released this in 1956. This is called Flying Saucer."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: Co-written with Bill Buchanan, this was a "break-in" song about an alien invasion, becoming a top 10 hit. It attracted significant attention, including lawsuits for copyright infringement, but Goodman and Buchanan were ultimately deemed to have created something new with their samples. "It was a lot more complicated in 1956 when goodman and his fellow songwriter bill bu cannon wrote a break in song about an alien invasion called flying saucer it was a top 10 hit."

srcs.episode: Ep. 44 - Streaking, Werewolves, Sharks, & Drinking - 70s Novelty Songs
